claims.text: phi is a Go terminal coding harness with file tools, subagents, diff review and on-demand MCP tool discovery.

evidence.quote:
A lean, high-performance terminal coding agent harness in Go — a sibling to Pi.

**Docs:** [pulseaiclub.github.io](https://pulseaiclub.github.io/)

- **Fast and small** — ~15 MB release binary, ~21 MB idle RSS, ~31 ms to first frame; no Node / Electron / Python runtime
- **Sub-agents** — spawn isolated jobs and watch the full run unfold in the TUI / job logs, without stuffing every turn into the parent context
- **Hashline edits** — edit by whole-file `@file path#TAG` plus line `LINE#HASH` anchors (same idea as [oh-my-pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi)): the model points at anchors instead of rewriting whole files; stale tags/hashes are rejected so over-edits and silent corruption stop here
- **Permission gate** — Gate / Ask before destructive tools fire; safety is not optional when an agent can touch your tree
- **MCP without context death** — configure as many MCP servers as you want; their tool schemas **never** enter the model prompt. The system prompt lists **server names** only (like the Skills catalog); the agent uses three meta-tools (`mcp_list` / `mcp_inspect` / `mcp_call`) to discover and call on demand. Same Gate / Ask / Hooks path as built-in tools. See [MCP](#mcp)
- **Extensions (Go or Rust)** — native binaries speak the **PXB** binary protocol over stdin/stdout; official author SDKs for Go ([`ext/go`](ext/go)) and Rust ([`ext/rust`](ext/rust)): LLM tools, slash commands, event intercepts, confirm dialogs — no reflection; JSON at the SDK edges via `serde_json`. See [Extensions](#extensions)
- **In-TUI diff review** — `/diff` opens a full-screen git review (working tree / staged / HEAD): syntax-highlighted hunks, line notes, then `a` sends notes to the agent. See [Diff review](#diff-review)
- **Any model** — OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, or Gemini via an explicit `api` field; built-in presets fill endpoint, context window, and capabilities for known model names (GPT, DeepSeek, Gemini, Kimi, GLM). See [Supported models](doc/models.md)

The TUI gives the model four core tools — `read`, `write`, `edit`, and
`bash` — plus `grep`, `find`, and `ls`. The model uses these to
fulfill your requests. External HTTP fetch is available via MCP when configured.

claims.text: Its optional optimizer sends history and context to TypeSafe for judging and ranking; the README does not identify a specific Jev model.

evidence.quote:
| `PHI_OPTIMIZER`  | Master on/off switch for optimizer features (`0`, `false`, `off`, `no` to disable) |
| `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` | TypeSafe API key required for optimizer features |

**Security:** When `PHI_OPTIMIZER` is enabled, command history and context are sent to an external TypeSafe service for judging and ranking. Avoid using the optimizer in environments where shell history may contain sensitive information (API keys, tokens, credentials).

claims.text: Configure a primary coding model with phi config, start phi, and supply TYPESAFE_API_KEY if enabling optimizer features.

evidence.quote:
First launch needs a model. Open the config editor (creates `~/.phi` layout
and writes `~/.phi/config.yaml`):

```sh
phi config
```

Or set env vars for a one-off run:

```sh
export PHI_MODEL=gpt-4o
export PHI_API_KEY=sk-...
```

Then start the TUI:

```sh
phi
```

| `PHI_OPTIMIZER`  | Master on/off switch for optimizer features (`0`, `false`, `off`, `no` to disable) |
| `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` | TypeSafe API key required for optimizer features |

it.title: phi — Programmazione da terminale con valutazioni TypeSafe facoltative
it.h1: phi — Programmazione da terminale con valutazioni TypeSafe facoltative
it.description: phi: L’ottimizzatore facoltativo invia cronologia e contesto a TypeSafe per valutare e ordinare; il README non identifica uno specifico modello Jev.
it.summary: phi è un ambiente di programmazione in Go con strumenti per file, sottoagenti, revisione delle differenze e scoperta MCP su richiesta. Configura il modello principale con phi config, avvia phi e fornisci TYPESAFE_API_KEY se attivi l’ottimizzatore.

sections.heading: A cosa serve
sections.text: phi è un ambiente di programmazione in Go con strumenti per file, sottoagenti, revisione delle differenze e scoperta MCP su richiesta.

sections.heading: Ruolo di Jev
sections.text: L’ottimizzatore facoltativo invia cronologia e contesto a TypeSafe per valutare e ordinare; il README non identifica uno specifico modello Jev.

sections.heading: Come iniziare
sections.text: Configura il modello principale con phi config, avvia phi e fornisci TYPESAFE_API_KEY se attivi l’ottimizzatore.

sections.heading: Ambito e limiti
sections.text: L’ottimizzatore trasferisce cronologia dei comandi e contesto a un servizio esterno. PHI_OPTIMIZER può disattivarlo; considera separatamente i dati sensibili nella cronologia.
